The surah opens with a most beloved address, and wherever the Muslims are addressed in this manner, it carries deep implications.

Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū (60:1) "O you who have believed!" This call comes from the Lord in whom they have believed. They are called by the name of the people of faith, so that they understand that their faith carries certain demands. You are standing at an extremely dangerous turning point; around you, enemies are weaving nets of conspiracy. And a very great responsibility has been placed upon you... in a manner of intimacy. Allah describes His enemies as the enemies of the believers and the enemies of the believers as His own enemies, so that the Muslims may have the awareness that they are the soldiers of Allah. It is towards Him that they must return. The enemy of Allah is their enemy.

Lā tattakhidhū ... bil-mawaddah (60:1) "Do not take My enemies and your enemies as friends, showing them affection, when they have disbelieved in the truth that has come to you..." Here the believers are given the awareness that they belong to Me and are coming towards Me. Therefore I am the enemy of your enemies. Hence they are people who are attributed to Allah, who raise the banners of Allah on this earth. They are the beloved and friends of Allah. Therefore it is not befitting for them to befriend the enemies of Allah. Here they are reminded: just consider what these enemies have done against you, what their attitude has been towards your religion and your Messenger. They persecuted you to the point of madness.

Wa qad kafarū ... bi-llāhi rabbikum (60:1) "And they have already disbelieved in the truth that has come to you, and their conduct is to expel the Messenger and you merely because you believe in Allah, your Lord." After such crimes, what foundation of friendship and love remains with them? They rejected the truth. They expelled the Messenger of Allah from his home and city. They expelled the believers, and their only offence was that they believed in Allah, the Lord of the worlds. The Muslims are being reminded of matters connected with their creed. Because of this very creed the polytheists waged war against them, and there was no other reason for that continuous war except this creed. It is being shown that the issue was indeed faith, on account of which such wars and enmities took place. This is a war of beliefs and a war of ideologies. The sole issue is that they denied the truth and expelled the Messenger and the Muslims because of their faith.

When this matter is clear and manifest, they are reminded that there is now no justification at all for showing them kindness and affection, provided you have come only for this purpose. If anyone has some other purpose, then he is not addressed by "Yā ayyuhā alladhīna āmanū" (60:1).

In su kuntum kharajtum jihādan fī sabīlī wa ibtighā'a marḍātī (60:1) "If you have gone forth to strive in My way and to seek My pleasure..." It is impossible that a person should have come out for jihad, emigrated for the sake of Allah's pleasure, and then been expelled on account of his faith, and yet love those who expelled him, while they are enemies of him and of Allah.

After this, they are warned about what lies secretly in their hearts: that they keep love for the enemies of Allah within their hearts, although nothing is hidden from Allah. He knows everything, both secret and open.

Tusirrūna ilayhim bil-mawaddah wa anā a'lamu bimā akhfaytum wa mā a'lantum (60:1) "You secretly send them messages of friendship, while I know well whatever you conceal and whatever you disclose."

After this they are threatened in a more severe manner, so severe that the heart of a believer trembles.

Wa man yaf'alhu minkum faqad ḍalla sawā'a l-sabīl (60:1) "Whoever among you does this has certainly strayed from the right path." The believer has given all his sacrifices for the sake of faith. If faith itself is threatened, what other danger can there be for him?

After these two warnings and admonitions, the believers are again told what the disbelievers think about them and what plans they make.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 2:

ان یثقفوکم .................... بالسوء (0 : 2) "Their attitude is that if they gain control over you, they will become your enemies and harm you with their hands and tongues." Whenever they find an opportunity against the Muslims, they display their baseness and enmity to the full. They inflict as much suffering on the believers as they are able to. Whether the harm is by hand or by tongue, they are ready for this task by every means and in every way... And the greatest thing, and the most frightening thing, is this:

وودوا لوتکفرون (06 : 2) "They wish that you would disbelieve." For sincere believers, this is a greater affliction than all other afflictions. Of every physical, verbal and spiritual affliction, this is the greatest for them, because through it a most precious treasure would slip from their hands: the treasure of faith, and they would become apostates. This would be the greatest enmity toward them.

The worth of this treasure is known only to the one who became a believer after disbelief, who saw the light of guidance after going astray, and who now lives the life of faith with his concepts, his thoughts and his consciousness, in complete tranquility. Such a person can in no way return to his former state. He dislikes disbelief just as he dislikes being thrown into fire. Therefore, the enemy of the believers is the one who wants to cast them back into the hell of disbelief, while Allah has granted them the ability to live in the paradise of faith. This makes faithful life full and meaningful, while the life of disbelief is empty and meaningless. Thus the Holy Quran gradually shows that the enemies of Muslims and of Allah want to make the believers disbelievers again; this is their fundamental scheme, and for this very reason you fled from Makkah. Take heed.

وودوا لوتکفرون (06 : 2) "And they wish that you would again become disbelievers."

This was the first stage, within which several truths, guidance and sharp prods to awakening were given. After this comes a stage in which a single keen realization is conveyed: that those kinship ties which compel a person toward secret friendship, and which make him forget a clear ideological stance, are of no benefit at all.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 3:

﴿Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. On that Day Allah will separate you [from one another], and Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (60:3)

The believer does good and seeks its reward in the Hereafter. He sows in this world and will reap in the Hereafter. This has an effect on him: when, in the Hereafter, there is no bond of faith and creed, then the bond of kinship will also be severed. Thus, in this brief life of the world, the importance of those ties of kinship and family relationship diminishes in his heart. He begins to attach importance to a bond that benefits him in both this world and the Hereafter and that endures, and that is the bond of ideology and faith.

﴿Neither your relatives nor your children will benefit you on the Day of Resurrection﴾ (60:3). These are the things toward which you lunge, and your hearts are attached to them, and these ties compel you to befriend your enemies so that you may preserve those ties, whereas Hatib did this for the sake of his children and property. Just as the hearts of others surge for their children and wealth, these things too will not benefit you. On the Day of Resurrection, ﴿Allah will separate you [from one another]﴾ (60:3), because the bond of kinship and the rope of relationship will be broken on that Day; on that Day only the rope of Allah will be effective.

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾ (60:3). He is aware of the outward, the inward, and even the intention.

Now comes the third paragraph. In it, the Muslim community is directed to its source, Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him). From Ibrahim onward there is one caravan and one community, which has continued through the long valleys of history. The provision of this caravan is the provision of faith. This caravan disassociates itself from every kind of relationship except the relationship of creed. This is the community that began with Ibrahim. He was Abu al-Anbiya (father of the prophets) and a caller to the religion of Hanif (pure monotheism). He is worthy of emulation, not only in creed but also in conduct and in the manner of preaching. He too faced this same issue of kinship and family ties. Thus Ibrahim and his believing companions left those relationships and lands behind and adopted only their creed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 4:

"There is indeed an excellent example for you in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: 'We are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone.'" [Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:4, in the form quoted here]

When a Muslim looks at history, he finds that his faith has a long genealogy and a lineage of belief. It extends far back into the past, to the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). Not only does he follow Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in his beliefs and convictions, but the da'wah (call to Islam) experiences of the people of faith and those of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) are also alike. Therefore, a believer is conscious that he possesses a vast store of experience: not only the experiences through which he is passing, but the experiences of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) are also included in it. The caravan of faith, which is now in Makkah, has travelled a very long way through the course of past history in time and space. It has crossed many valleys. It has walked only under this one banner, and has passed through the same kinds of circumstances through which these people are passing. This is not a new matter, as though only you have been afflicted with these hardships. If the believers have now been cut off from their enemies, what of it? They are a branch of an ideology whose very shady branches have spread far and wide across the atmosphere of history. This is the tree whose sapling was planted by Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

Ibrahim (peace be upon him) too passed through the same kind of experience that the Muslims were passing through in Madinah, and in Ibrahim (peace be upon him) there is an excellent example (uswah hasanah) for the people of faith.

"Indeed there is for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: 'Indeed we are free of you and of what you worship besides Allah. We have rejected you, and enmity and hatred have appeared between us and you forever, until you believe in Allah alone.'" In this, they declared their disassociation from their people, their deities, and their worship. In other words, they rejected disbelief and believed in Allah, and this enmity and hostility does not end until they believe in Allah alone. This was a clear, decisive and firm severing of ties, after which every kind of connection between the two parties was cut off, except the bond of faith. This same decision is the decision of the people of faith, and this is the resolution of those believers who are in Madinah. And it should be so, just as the community of Ibrahim decided.

Some believers used to see that Ibrahim (peace be upon him), despite severing ties, sought forgiveness for his father, although he was a mushrik. In this there was a way for some Muslims to stir up suppressed feelings they harboured for their polytheist brethren. Therefore the Qur'an clarified the meaning of Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) seeking forgiveness, for he had said to his father:

"I will surely ask forgiveness for you" [Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:4]. He said this at a time when his father had not persisted in shirk. This was at a time when he still had hope regarding his father's faith.

"And when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of Allah, he disassociated himself from him" [Surah al-Tawbah 9:114], as has come in another surah.

Here it is shown that Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had entrusted the whole matter to Allah and had turned to Allah with reliance and single-mindedness.

"And I have no power to obtain anything from Allah for you. Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned, and to You is the final return" [Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:4-5]. Thus the declaration of complete submission to Allah is a distinguishing feature of the character of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). And here the hearts of the people of faith are directed towards it, because the Qur'an's method is to take a single link of a story, analyse it, and direct the people of faith towards it, and to clarify, within that link, the lesson, admonition, wisdom and exemplary model that Muslims can follow.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 5:

In the course of this narrative, this part of Ibrahim's supplication is also important.

﴿Our Lord, make us not a trial for the disbelievers﴾ (60:5). "Do not let these disbelievers dominate us, for that domination would become a trial for the disbelievers. They would say: if the Muslims were upon the truth, and their faith could protect them, how would we have prevailed over them?" These same doubts arise in the hearts of the believers in every age, when the people of falsehood and the people of disbelief prevail over the believers. Rebels and transgressors prevail over the believers, and there is wisdom of Allah in this as well. This dominance is for a time. The believer endures these trials. Yet even in such circumstances, the believers should supplicate that Allah not place them in such trials.

﴿Our Lord, forgive us﴾ (60:5). "Our Lord, forgive our sins." Ibrahim, the Khalil of Allah (Khalil Allah), makes this supplication, because he knows that the lofty station of servitude to Allah is difficult to attain, and that no human being can render to Allah the servitude that is equal to His bounties and His favours, or that is worthy of His purity and majesty. Therefore he supplicates so that this would be an example for those who come after him.

Your supplication, your turning to Allah, your seeking forgiveness, and your praise of the Lord conclude thus:

﴿Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (60:5). You have power over everything, and all Your affairs are based on wisdom.

It is said about the conduct of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his companions that there is an excellent example in it for you, who turned to Allah in the most difficult circumstances and submitted before Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 6:

"There is certainly an excellent example for you in them, for everyone who hopes for Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away, then indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy." (60:6)

Therefore, Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his companions are an example for the one who hopes in Allah and is concerned about accountability before the Hereafter. Only such people can value the experiences of Hazrat Ibrahim in their hearts, and only they can take them as a model and exemplar. And by observing them, one can find guidance. Therefore, those whose aims are Allah and the Hereafter should look at the example of Hazrat Ibrahim (peace be upon him). This is an indication to the believers.

But those who do not care for the Islamic system, and who wish to deviate from the caravan of Ibrahim's path, and whoever wishes to distance himself from this lineage, then Allah has no need of him.

"Indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy." (60:6) From this journey we now return. The believers have studied their history. Now they return to the earth carrying their memories. The instructive experiences that they had from the earlier nations, they gathered together, and what decisions those among the earlier nations who passed through similar circumstances had made, they learned, and they realised that the path on which they were walking is one on which people have walked before. They are not the first people who have done this work.

The Qur'an is firmly planting this conception in the hearts of the caravan of the Muslims so that this caravan keeps moving, and so that it does not feel that it is alone or unique, even though in the present generation it is alone. In this way it receives support, and the hardship of walking on this path becomes less. Although the path is difficult and rugged, many people have walked on it before and passed through these same defiles.

Amid the state of war that existed between Makkah and Madinah, in which brother had been cut off from brother, and people found this situation extremely burdensome, a ray of hope is now shown: that this situation is due to the obstinacy of the people of Makkah, and it can be hoped that eventually these people too will join this caravan. Let them take up that same banner. In this way it will be possible for the bond of brotherhood to be restored as well. Now further clarification is given, and a permanent rule of international law is stated: that the boycott, enmity and hostility between Muslims and disbelievers is directed toward those who are enemies of Islam. And if someone gives up enmity toward Islam, then every Muslim is permitted to show kindness to whomever he wishes and who deserves kindness, and just and equitable relations should be established between them.

Islam is a religion of peace and the creed of love. It is a system that wishes to embrace the entire world under its protective shade, and the whole world wishes to establish its own way of life. It gathers people under the banners of Allah and makes them brothers who know one another. If there is any obstacle in this path, it is that the enemies of Islam carry out their hostile activities. They oppose Islam and the followers of Islam. If the opponents of Islam, Islam and the people of Islam, give up their enmity, then Islam has no interest in enmity with anyone. Islam does not create enmity of its own accord. Even in enmity and a state of war, it does not cut the causes of affection and love in human souls. It deals justly and always remains hopeful that all people will gather under the banner of Islam. Islam never despairs of anyone's guidance and returning to the right path.

In the first verse of this section is mention of that hope, which is never overcome by despair. This verse is a balm for the hearts of those upon whom Islam and disbelief imposed that war, and who were compelled to cut off relations with their relatives.

﴿Perhaps Allah will bring about affection between you and those with whom you have made enmity today﴾ (60:7). The expression of hope from Allah is, as it were, a definite indication that this enmity would soon end. The believers who heard it must have become certain. Soon after, Makkah was conquered, all the people of Makkah became Muslims, and all came under one banner. All the records of those enmities and hostilities were rolled up, and the people of Makkah and the people of Madinah became like brothers.

﴿And Allah is Powerful﴾ (60:7): He does what He wills.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (60:7): He who had associated partners with Him in the past period and in the state of disbelief, He forgives him. He forgives the sins of the past period.

Until the promise of Allah, about which hope was given in the verse above, is fulfilled, Allah permitted the establishment of relations of friendship with those who were not at war with Muslims regarding religion and who had not expelled Muslims from their homes. The prohibition that was considered applicable to doing good to such people was lifted, so that one should act justly even with such disbelievers, and if their right lies within your authority, fulfill it. But those who are fighting you regarding religion, who have expelled you from your homes, or have assisted in your expulsion, with such people there is no alliance (muwalat), and those who make alliance with such people are wrongdoers. One of the meanings of zulm (wrongdoing) is also shirk (association of partners with Allah). The verse: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice﴾ (31:13) should be kept in view. For the believers, this is a severe warning, so they should be very cautious while establishing such relations, lest they lose everything.

This principle that has been laid down regarding relations with non-Muslims is in accordance with the temperament of this religion and is a most just international law. It is from a purely human point of view, and it has been framed keeping in view the system of this entire universe, because this entire universe is created by the one God. This entire universe is oriented toward the one Lord, and the entire universe is moving according to Allah's plan, system and design, even though there are differences among people within it and they are divided among themselves.

This principle is the fundamental principle of Islam's international law, according to which the state of peace and security among people is the original and permanent state, and this state changes due to aggression and defense against aggression, or because of a treaty between two nations, where one of them breaks the treaty or the possibility of betrayal arises, or some power stands as an obstacle to freedom of belief, freedom of expression and the call to Islam. And this too is in reality a form of aggression. Apart from these circumstances, Islam gives commands of peace and security, love, goodness and justice.

This rule is in exact accordance with the Islamic worldview, because Islam distinguishes between person and person only on the basis of creed. If a believer fights against another nation, he does so only because of his creed. There is no other reason for war. Islam fights only for freedom of the call and freedom of opinion. Beyond this, it fights only for the establishment of the Islamic system and the elevation of the word of Allah.

This explanation and interpretation is also consistent with the overall direction of this entire surah, in which the importance of beliefs and ideologies is discussed, and it is shown that the believers can fight only under an ideological banner. Therefore, whoever stands with them in this front is one of them, and whoever fights them on this point is their enemy. Whoever maintained a state of peace with them and left them upon their beliefs, so that they could call people to their beliefs, and did not try to block their path, and did not forcibly prevent people from accepting Islamic beliefs, is a peaceful party (musalim), and Islam does not prevent doing good to them and establishing social relations with them.

The fact is that a Muslim lives on this earth for the sake of his creed. His problem is his ideology, and his problem with his environment is also this same ideology. Therefore, he has no quarrel with anyone over interests and benefits. He does not fight for any partisanship, such as partisanship of color, race, language and region. In Islam, if there is war, it is only for ideologies, so that the word of Allah may be raised, and it is war for the Islamic system.

After this, Surah al-Tawbah was revealed, in which is: ﴿A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger toward those of the polytheists﴾ (9:1). By this, treaties with polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula were terminated. Those whose treaty had no fixed term were given a respite of four months, and with those whose treaty had a fixed term, a period of the treaty was determined. But the treaties of peace that were with the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula and that were annulled, were so because the polytheists of Arabia were repeatedly breaking their agreements. When it benefited them they would abide by the agreement, and when it harmed them they would break it. Therefore, Islam made another international rule for such people.

﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, throw back to them [their treaty] openly, [and deal equally]. Indeed, Allah does not like the treacherous﴾ (8:58). This necessity also arose at that time so that the capital and center of Islam could be secured. At that time the center of Islam was the Arabian Peninsula, and it was necessary to cleanse it of those who were constantly waiting for an opportunity to attack Muslims. The polytheists and the People of the Book, bound by treaties, had repeatedly broken their covenant. Since by its nature this is a state of hostility, in such circumstances it is beneficial for both parties to be in a state of war. Especially in circumstances where the great empires of Caesar and Chosroes had begun gathering armies against the Islamic state, and both had regarded Islam as a threat to themselves. Both had turned the Arab states toward the Arabian Peninsula along with the Arabian Peninsula itself. Therefore, the internal purification of the Islamic bloc became necessary so that the anticipated external aggression could be effectively confronted. This note is sufficient here.

﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (60:7): He who had associated partners with Him in the past period and in the state of disbelief, He forgives him. He forgives the sins of the past period.

Until the promise of Allah, about which hope was given in the verse above, is fulfilled, Allah permitted the establishment of relations of friendship with those who were not at war with Muslims regarding religion and who had not expelled Muslims from their homes. The prohibition that was considered applicable to doing good to such people was lifted, so that one should act justly even with such disbelievers, and if their right lies within your authority, fulfill it. But those who are fighting you regarding religion, who have expelled you from your homes, or have assisted in your expulsion, with such people there is no alliance (muwalat), and those who make alliance with such people are wrongdoers. One of the meanings of zulm (wrongdoing) is also shirk (association of partners with Allah). The verse: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is great injustice﴾ (31:13) should be kept in view. For the believers, this is a severe warning, so they should be very cautious while establishing such relations, lest they lose everything.

This principle that has been laid down regarding relations with non-Muslims is in accordance with the temperament of this religion and is a most just international law. It is from a purely human point of view, and it has been framed keeping in view the system of this entire universe, because this entire universe is created by the one God. This entire universe is oriented toward the one Lord, and the entire universe is moving according to Allah's plan, system and design, even though there are differences among people within it and they are divided among themselves.

This principle is the fundamental principle of Islam's international law, according to which the state of peace and security among people is the original and permanent state, and this state changes due to aggression and defense against aggression, or because of a treaty between two nations, where one of them breaks the treaty or the possibility of betrayal arises, or some power stands as an obstacle to freedom of belief, freedom of expression and the call to Islam. And this too is in reality a form of aggression. Apart from these circumstances, Islam gives commands of peace and security, love, goodness and justice.

This rule is in exact accordance with the Islamic worldview, because Islam distinguishes between person and person only on the basis of creed. If a believer fights against another nation, he does so only because of his creed. There is no other reason for war. Islam fights only for freedom of the call and freedom of opinion. Beyond this, it fights only for the establishment of the Islamic system and the elevation of the word of Allah.

This explanation and interpretation is also consistent with the overall direction of this entire surah, in which the importance of beliefs and ideologies is discussed, and it is shown that the believers can fight only under an ideological banner. Therefore, whoever stands with them in this front is one of them, and whoever fights them on this point is their enemy. Whoever maintained a state of peace with them and left them upon their beliefs, so that they could call people to their beliefs, and did not try to block their path, and did not forcibly prevent people from accepting Islamic beliefs, is a peaceful party (musalim), and Islam does not prevent doing good to them and establishing social relations with them.

The fact is that a Muslim lives on this earth for the sake of his creed. His problem is his ideology, and his problem with his environment is also this same ideology. Therefore, he has no quarrel with anyone over interests and benefits. He does not fight for any partisanship, such as partisanship of color, race, language and region. In Islam, if there is war, it is only for ideologies, so that the word of Allah may be raised, and it is war for the Islamic system.

After this, Surah al-Tawbah was revealed, in which is: ﴿A declaration of disassociation from Allah and His Messenger toward those of the polytheists﴾ (9:1). By this, treaties with polytheists in the Arabian Peninsula were terminated. Those whose treaty had no fixed term were given a respite of four months, and with those whose treaty had a fixed term, a period of the treaty was determined. But the treaties of peace that were with the polytheists of the Arabian Peninsula and that were annulled, were so because the polytheists of Arabia were repeatedly breaking their agreements. When it benefited them they would abide by the agreement, and when it harmed them they would break it. Therefore, Islam made another international rule for such people.

﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, throw back to them [their treaty] openly, [and deal equally]. Indeed, Allah does not like the treacherous﴾ (8:58). This necessity also arose at that time so that the capital and center of Islam could be secured. At that time the center of Islam was the Arabian Peninsula, and it was necessary to cleanse it of those who were constantly waiting for an opportunity to attack Muslims. The polytheists and the People of the Book, bound by treaties, had repeatedly broken their covenant. Since by its nature this is a state of hostility, in such circumstances it is beneficial for both parties to be in a state of war. Especially in circumstances where the great empires of Caesar and Chosroes had begun gathering armies against the Islamic state, and both had regarded Islam as a threat to themselves. Both had turned the Arab states toward the Arabian Peninsula along with the Arabian Peninsula itself. Therefore, the internal purification of the Islamic bloc became necessary so that the anticipated external aggression could be effectively confronted. This note is sufficient here.

Now we turn to the context of the surah: the matter of the believing women who emigrate.

"O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them. Allah knows best their faith. Then if you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for them. And give the disbelievers what they have spent (as dower). There is no blame on you in marrying them when you have paid them their dowers. And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women; ask back what you have spent as dower, and let the disbelievers ask back what they have spent. That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise. And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers and you are then given a turn, pay to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent. And fear Allah, in whom you believe."

Regarding the occasion of revelation of these verses, it is reported that the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah were as follows: "No person from among us will come to you who is upon your religion, but you will return him to us." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims were still in the low-lying area of Hudaybiyyah, some believing women came, seeking emigration and wishing to reach the Abode of Islam. The Quraysh came, demanding that they be returned in accordance with the agreement. From the wording of the agreement it appears that it said nothing about women. Then these verses were revealed, forbidding the return of emigrant women, because women are weak and could be exposed to trial regarding their religion.

With their emigration, the international rulings of this matter also came into force. This legislation was also carried out in an extremely just manner, and no consideration was given to the transgressions of the opposing party, because Islam does not base any law, in internal or external affairs, upon vindictive emotions.

In this regard, Islam's first step was to examine the circumstances of these women, to see for what purpose they were emigrating. Lest they wished to escape from their former husbands, or were seeking some benefit, or lest they were following some beloved person into the Abode of Islam.

Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said that they were made to take an oath that they had not come out out of enmity toward their husbands. They were also made to swear that they had not set out, weary of Makkah, towards the land of Madinah. They were made to swear that they had not come for some other worldly interest. And they were made to swear that they had not come under any impulse other than love of Allah and His Messenger. And they were made to swear that they had not come under any impulse other than love of Allah and His Messenger.

Ikrimah said that the oath also included: "You are coming only out of love for Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); you have no love for any man among the Muslims; and you are not trying to flee from your husband?"

This was their test. Relying upon their outward circumstances, their verbal declaration under oath was accepted. As for what is in their hearts, only Allah is aware of it. There is no way for a human being to know the secrets of hearts.

"Allah knows best their faith" (60:10): if they affirm this matter by sworn statement, then—

"Do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for them" (60:10).

In fact, a superior bond has come into play: the bond of faith, which has severed all other relationships. Thus no bond remains that could join what has been separated. The marital bond is such that two persons blend together with one another, become joined, and a permanent and lasting relationship is established. When there is no unity of faith between the spouses, it is not possible to fulfill the rights of marriage. Faith is the name of a higher life of the heart, and no other feeling can take its place. Without the bond of faith, unity and harmony between husband and wife are not possible; neither affection nor intimacy can arise between the parties, whereas love, mutual tenderness, and peace and tranquility are essential between husband and wife.

In the early period of the Hijrah this ruling had not yet come. A believing woman and a disbelieving man were not separated, nor was a believing man separated from a disbelieving woman, because in that period the Islamic social order and Islamic society were not yet firmly established. But after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, or the Conquest of Hudaybiyyah, according to most reports, a decision was made that a marital relationship between a believer and a disbeliever should no longer remain. The marital relationship should be only between believing men and believing women. As the practical situation had become, only the bond of faith remained, and in Madinah there was only the bond of faith. Only the relationship with Allah and His Messenger remained, and all other kinds of relationships had been severed and uprooted from their very foundations.

But after this separation, just legislation was enacted for the party that suffered loss. If a ruling of separation was issued for the wife of a disbelieving husband, then what he had given her as dower, or other expenses he had incurred, had to be returned to him. Likewise, if a disbelieving woman was separated from a Muslim man, the dower and maintenance that the Muslim man had given were returned to him.

Now, the marriage of believing men with emigrant believing women was declared lawful, on condition that they pay them their dowers. There is a jurisprudential difference of opinion as to whether these women had to observe the waiting period (iddah). Only pregnant women were required to observe it, that is, until delivery. If there is an 'iddah, is it the 'iddah of a divorced woman, that is, three menstrual cycles (tuhr), or is a single menstruation together with certainty that the womb is clear sufficient? (See the books of fiqh.)

"And give them what they have spent" (60:10): "Give back to the disbelievers what they had spent. There is no blame on you in marrying them when you have paid them their dowers. And do not hold on to marriage with disbelieving women; ask back what you have spent as dower, and let the disbelievers ask back what they have spent" (60:10). After this, Allah appoints Himself the guarantor and watchman over the implementation of all these rulings, which is in the heart of every Muslim: that Allah is watching; fear Allah.

"That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise" (60:10). This is the sole guarantee on which one can rely, that no one will commit deceit, trickery, or breach of covenant, for the rulings of Allah are the rulings of the All-Knowing, the All-Aware. These are the rulings of the Judge who knows even the secrets of hearts. These rulings belong to the Ruler who is most mighty and possessed of all powers. For a Muslim's conscience this connection alone is sufficient, and he knows where this ruling has come from, so he follows these rulings and observes them, because the believer is certain that he will go before Allah.

Now, if Muslims had given their wives dower etc., and those wives remained in the Abode of Disbelief, where by this law they had become separated, and their families or guardians did not return the Muslims' right, as indeed happened in practice in some circumstances, then the ruler of the time will compensate their loss from a fund which belongs to those disbelievers whose wives have come to the Abode of Islam, or payment will be made from the amounts that came to the Muslims from the disbelievers as booty.

"And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers and you are then given a turn, pay to those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent" (60:11).

And the carrying out of this command is also tied to faith, because in Islam every command is connected with Allah.

"And fear Allah, in whom you believe" (60:11). For those who believe in Allah, this is a very effective reminder.

Thus these rulings establish, between spouses, a realistic dissolution of marriage, and this separation accords with the Islamic conception of life. Islam holds a distinct conception regarding marital ties. Islam wishes that Islamic ranks be completely separate and distinguished from other ranks, that the whole of life be founded upon the Islamic outlook on life, and that it be bound to the axis of faith, and that a human society be formed in which there is no collective system based on race, color, language, lineage, land, or regional foundations, and in which there is only one banner by which people are differentiated: namely, the party that belongs to the people of Allah, which is the Party of Allah (ḥizb Allah), and the party that belongs to Satan, which is called the Party of Satan (ḥizb al-shayṭān).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 12:

After this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told on what matters these women who have migrated will be made to pledge allegiance. The pledge of these women, or of those women who wish to enter Islam, will be as follows:

"O Prophet, when believing women come to you to pledge allegiance, on the condition that they will not associate anything with Allah, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill their children, will not bring forth any slander they have fabricated between their hands and feet, and will not disobey you in any right matter, then accept their pledge and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." (60:12)

These matters on which women are made to pledge allegiance are the fundamental elements of the Islamic outlook on life, and they are also the foundational principles of collective life.

1. That they will not associate anyone with Allah in any way. 2. That they will not steal (sariqah). 3. That they will abstain from adultery (zina). 4. That they will not kill their children.

In the Jahiliyyah it was customary to bury women alive. This also includes killing the unborn child (janin), for whatever reason. This is because they are trustees of the unborn child.

"Nor bring forth any slander they have fabricated between their hands and feet" (60:12). Ibn Abbas explained its meaning as: that they will not attribute to their husbands a child belonging to someone other than those husbands. Muqatil also holds this opinion.

This protection against the commission of adultery is a necessary instruction following the pledge. In the Jahiliyyah it was the custom that women would form illicit sexual relations with several men. When a child was born, they would assign it to the man with whom it bore resemblance. Sometimes they would attach the child to another person, although they knew who its father was.

However, the general words of the verse include all circumstances in which slander is involved. The reason Ibn Abbas and Muqatil restricted it is that at that time there were circumstances that were being abolished by the prohibition of adultery, but the question of attaching children to pregnant women had to be decided in any case.

"Nor disobey you in any right matter" (60:12). This refers to obedience to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in every matter that he asks of them. And it is clear that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will only command what is right. However, the word "right" (ma'ruf) has been added here because it is a constitutional provision. In the Islamic constitution, the fundamental principle is that obedience to rulers is limited within a bounded sphere. Obedience to rulers is obligatory only in those matters which conform to the Islamic Shariah. In Islam there is no principle of absolute obedience. According to the Islamic constitution, the source of the authority for legislation and governance is the Islamic Shariah. Neither the will of the Imam of the time, nor the will of the people, nor any majority or collective principle can give the status of law to anything that contradicts the Shariah. Therefore, both the people and the Imam of the people are bound by the Islamic Shariah.

When these women have pledged allegiance, then they become believing women, and then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will pray for their forgiveness, that Allah may pardon their previous sins.

"Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" (60:12). He is the one who pardons shortcomings.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 60, verse 13:

The Concluding Striking Remark:

"O you who believe, do not take as friends a people upon whom Allah has been wrathful, who have despaired of the Hereafter just as the disbelievers in the graves have despaired." (60:13)

Some narrations state that the people referred to here are the Jews, upon whom Allah's wrath has descended. The evidence offered for this is that in several places in the Qur'an these words are used for this people. However, the verse may also be general, so that its meaning includes those who are polytheists, who are mentioned throughout this surah, and all of Allah's enemies may be intended. This is because all the enemies of Allah have despaired of the Hereafter and attach no importance to it. And they are compared to the disbelievers who are in the graves. They have come to know that they committed disbelief and polytheism; now they are eternal inhabitants of Hellfire. The period of worldly respite has ended. Now in the gathering there is only reckoning, and they are to fall into Hell.

This final call encompasses the calls and invitations of the entire surah. Thus the surah begins and ends with the same theme: do not take as friends those upon whom Allah is wrathful, and within this conclusion the whole voice of the surah has been gathered.
